entries.risk_area: HTML injection / Semgrep replaceAll escaping audit
entries.evidence: All attacker-derived strings interpolated into email HTML are passed through escapeHtml, which encodes &, <, >, double quote and apostrophe before text-node insertion; templates contain no attacker-controlled raw HTML, URL attributes, CSS or JavaScript contexts. The four Semgrep matches are chained replaceAll audit warnings for this same context-appropriate control, not bypass evidence.

The write destination is formed from crypto.randomUUID() plus path.extname(file.name).toLowerCase().slice(0,10), not the original filename; extname extracts an extension without filesystem separators, and the UUID prevents a dot-segment basename. This is the only destination construction before fs.writeFile in the helper. No current callers were found, but that absence is not the basis of closure.

Public inquiry endpoint has no authentication/session/JWT, persisted user object, tenant, or user-selected private record. Handler constructs explicit contact fields and sends email; it cannot cross account/object boundaries that do not exist.

Route consumes no cookies, HTTP authentication, authorization token, or victim-associated persisted state. Cross-origin public submissions carry the same anonymous authority available by direct submission; missing origin validation is not an authenticated CSRF vulnerability.
